newsitem.title: PERU: Gunshots fired into air at Peru siege - witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Gunshots fired into air at Peru siege - witnesses.

text.p: Three gunshots were heard on Tuesday at the besieged Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima where Marxist rebels held 74 hostages.
Witnesses on the roof of a neighboring house said the shots were apparently fired into the air by a gun from outside the residence.

"Each one sounded like a low thud as if they came from a silenced gun. They passed over so close I could hear them sizzling," said Gregg Newton, a Reuters photographer on the roof overlooking the residence.
Cameramen on the roof said the shots were fired as they stood up to change places.
There was no immediate comment about the shots from policemen at the site.

Gunshots heard at the residence previously during the 28-day siege have been attributed to a desire on the part of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding the hostages to make their presence felt. On Monday, the guerrillas fired three bursts of gunfire into the air.
